paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: a fiery trial is not a sign that something went wrong. Peter says, "do not be surprised at the fiery trial that has come upon you, as though something strange were happening to you" (1 Peter 4:12). I bet most of us think hard times mean we missed a turn somewhere, like a GPS that keeps saying "recalculating." But Peter says when you suffer for Christ, you share in His sufferings, and that leads to being "overjoyed at the revelation of His glory" (1 Peter 4:13).

So what does that do for the baker standing in the heat? It means the insult is not the end of the story. Peter says, "If you are insulted for the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you" (1 Peter 4:14). Don't be ashamed of the name Christian, and glorify God that you bear it (1 Peter 4:16). Just make sure you're suffering for that name, and not for something like being a thief or a meddler (1 Peter 4:15). Yes, I felt that one in my mustache.

And when the heat stays on, Peter tells you where to put your soul. Those who suffer according to God's will "should entrust their souls to their faithful Creator and continue to do good" (1 Peter 4:19). That's it. You hand yourself over to the One who made you and doesn't let go, then you keep baking the good stuff. Don't stop doing good just because the oven is hot, friend. He is faithful, and He is holding you.
